headline: Commission issues forced labour guidance as CSRD enforcement priorities emerge
summary: The European Commission published official implementation guidelines for the EU Forced Labour Regulation, directly affecting Chinese supply chains. Simultaneously, ESMA set 2026 sustainability enforcement priorities, and reports indicated limits on supplier data requests under EU reporting frameworks. Clarifications were also issued regarding EUDR product scopes.

items.title: Commission publishes official guidelines on EU Forced Labour Regulation
items.what: The European Commission released official implementation guidelines detailing enforcement expectations, risk identification, and due diligence under the EU Forced Labour Regulation.
items.meaning: Crucial for power tool and battery production in China; outlines the evidence required to prevent supply chain investigations and potential EU border import bans.
items.action: Benchmark Chinese supplier audit procedures and battery component traceability against the new Commission guidance.

sources.title: Update on the EU Forced Labour Regulation: The European Commission's Guidelines Have Been Published

items.title: ESMA and national regulators establish 2026 CSRD enforcement priorities
items.what: ESMA set its 2026 European common enforcement priorities, highlighting double materiality assessments and connectivity between financial and sustainability disclosures, endorsed by national authorities including France's AMF.
items.meaning: As a listed brand preparing CSRD statements, materiality methodology and data sourced from Chinese suppliers will face rigorous regulatory scrutiny.
items.action: Ensure supply chain data collection aligns directly with documented double materiality outcomes.

sources.title: EU Sustainability reporting – ESMA sets 2026 common enforcement priorities – materiality and providing connected information remain firmly in focus
Preparing upcoming sustainability statements: the AMF draws listed companies’ attention to ESMA’s 2026 recommendations

items.title: Reported data ceiling allows mid-sized suppliers to decline excess ESG requests
items.what: Reports indicate EU rules establish boundaries permitting suppliers with up to 1,000 employees to push back against excessive sustainability data demands from corporate buyers.
items.meaning: May restrict the depth of bespoke sustainability questionnaires your Chinese manufacturing partners are obliged to complete for your CSRD disclosures.
items.action: Standardise supplier requests around mandatory ESRS core metrics rather than expansive bespoke questionnaires.

sources.title: Brussels Sets a Data Ceiling: Suppliers With Up to 1,000 Staff Can Now Refuse Extra Sustainability R

items.title: EU clarifies and narrows Deforestation Regulation scope for manufactured goods
items.what: Reports state the EU clarified and narrowed product scopes under the EU Deforestation Regulation, specifically addressing derived products including rubber and wooden items.
items.meaning: Affects imports of garden tools, rubber components (such as tool grips and wheels), and wooden or cardboard packaging ahead of statutory application.
items.action: Screen imported finished product codes and packaging materials against the clarified EUDR customs lists.

sources.title: EU Narrows and Clarifies Deforestation Rules Affecting Furniture, Rubber and Other Goods

items.title: PEFC amends trademark rules to meet EU green claims standards
items.what: PEFC updated its certification and trademark rules to ensure alignment with the EU Empowering Consumers for the Green Transition Directive.
items.meaning: On-pack environmental claims and certified wood or cardboard packaging must comply with the revised rules to avoid greenwashing sanctions.
items.action: Verify that consumer packaging using PEFC logos complies with the revised certification guidelines.

sources.title: PEFC amends trademark rules to align with EU EmpCo requirements
